text: You just rolled over in bed, and now the whole room is spinning.
Deep in your ear sits a tiny pouch full of even tinier stones.
These ear rocks help you feel which way is up.
Right next to them are three loops filled with fluid.
When you turn your head, that fluid sloshes and bends tiny hairs.
Those hairs tell your brain how fast you're turning.
But sometimes a few ear rocks break loose and fall into a loop.
Now every time you move, they keep rolling after your head stops.
Your ears scream that you're spinning, but your eyes say you're not.
It feels like a ride you can't get off, for up to a minute.
A doctor can tip your head just right to roll the rocks back out.
Subscribe, because that's what really causes vertigo.
